title: Mechanical Fitter Salary Guide: Hourly to Annual Pay for 38-Hour Weeks
description: Calculate a mechanical fitter salary from hourly rates under the Manufacturing Award. Includes 38-hour weeks, fortnightly pay, casual loading, super, and tax estimates for 2026–27.
salarySummary: A mechanical fitter under the Manufacturing Award (C10 classification) earns a minimum hourly rate above the National Minimum Wage of $26.44, with annual pay calculated as hourly × 38 × 52.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for a mechanical fitter in 2026?
faqs.a: Mechanical fitters are typically classified as C10 – Engineering/manufacturing tradesperson level I under the Manufacturing and Associated Industries and Occupations Award. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. The exact C10 rate is published in the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides; it is higher than the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour. For the most current rate, check the Manufacturing Award pay guide on the Fair Work Ombudsman website.

faqs.q: How is a mechanical fitter salary calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Use the formula: annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52. For a full-time mechanical fitter, assume 38 ordinary hours per week. For example, at $30 per hour: $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280 per year. Fortnightly pay is weekly pay × 2 ($1,140 × 2 = $2,280). This calculation assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

faqs.q: Does casual loading apply to a mechanical fitter salary?
faqs.a: Yes. Casual mechanical fitters are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate under the Manufacturing Award. For example, if the base rate is $30 per hour, the casual rate is $37.50 per hour. The loading is paid instead of entitlements like paid leave. Superannuation is still paid on top of the casual rate at 12% of ordinary earnings.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the mechanical fitter salary

If you are a mechanical fitter or considering a role in this trade, knowing how to convert an hourly rate into an annual salary is essential. The **mechanical fitter salary** depends on the award classification, your experience, and whether you work full-time, part-time, or casually. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year to give you clear estimates.

### Award coverage for mechanical fitters

Mechanical fitters in Australia are generally covered by the **Manufacturing and Associated Industries and Occupations Award** (MA000010). The most common classification is **C10 – Engineering/manufacturing tradesperson level I**. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes updated pay guides each year after the Annual Wage Review. From 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. The National Minimum Wage also rose to $26.44 per hour, but award rates for skilled trades like mechanical fitting are higher.

To find the exact minimum rate for a mechanical fitter, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website. The Manufacturing Award pay guide lists all classification rates, including penalty rates and allowances.

### The formula: hourly to annual

Annual gross pay = **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full-time mechanical fitter, we assume **38 ordinary hours per week** (the standard under the National Employment Standards and most awards).

**Example:** If your hourly rate is $30.00 per hour:
- Weekly: $30.00 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Fortnightly: $1,140.00 × 2 = $2,280.00
- Annual: $30.00 × 38 × 52 = **$59,280.00

This is the gross annual figure before tax and before super. The same formula works for any hourly rate. If you are a casual mechanical fitter, you add 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. Do not include the loading in the base rate you enter into a calculator; the loading is applied separately.

### Casual loading and superannuation

Casual employees under the Manufacturing Award receive a **25% casual loading** on the ordinary hourly rate. For the example above, the casual rate would be $37.50 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your gross earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is **12% of ordinary earnings**, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time mechanical fitter earning $59,280, super would be $59,280 × 12% = $7,113.60 per year, paid by the employer on top of your salary.

### Tax and Medicare levy

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the **Medicare levy** of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). For a mechanical fitter earning $59,280, the estimated tax is approximately $7,000–$8,000, and Medicare about $1,185. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a personalised estimate.

### Comparing the mechanical fitter salary with averages

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week, or about $108,352 per year. This is higher than a typical mechanical fitter award rate, reflecting many roles above the minimum. However, the award minimum provides a solid baseline. For more context, see the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

### Fortnightly pay and budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Your fortnightly gross is simply weekly pay × 2. For a $30 per hour mechanical fitter: $1,140 × 2 = $2,280. After tax and Medicare, your fortnightly take-home might be around $1,900–$2,000 depending on your tax withholding. This helps with budgeting rent, bills, and savings.

### Key distinctions

- **National Minimum Wage**: $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026). This is the legal floor for award-free employees. Mechanical fitters under an award earn more.
- **Award rate**: The Manufacturing Award minimum for a C10 tradesperson is higher than the NMW. Check the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for comparisons.
- **Casual loading**: 25% on top of the base rate, not included in the base.
- **Super**: 12% paid on top of ordinary earnings, not deducted from your pay.

### Using the timesheet calculator

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then shows your weekly, fortnightly and annual gross pay. It does not include penalty rates or allowances. For a mechanical fitter working standard hours, it gives a clear picture of your regular earnings.

### Summary

A mechanical fitter salary is straightforward to estimate: hourly rate × 38 × 52. Remember to add super on top and deduct tax and Medicare for your net pay. Always check the latest pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman for your exact classification. For more details on salary packaging and super, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).
